hints: Focus on what actually makes the pollutant here, the sulfur impurity burning in oxygen to form sulfur dioxide.
Start by converting the mass of sulfur to moles using $A_r = 32.1$, then remember the burning equation gives a 1 to 1 mole link to $\text{SO}_2$.
To finish, multiply your moles of $\text{SO}_2$ by the room conditions molar volume, $24000 \text{ cm}^3 \text{ mol}^{-1}$, and see which volume you get.
walkthrough:
**Write the burning equation for sulfur**

Every sulfur atom ends up in one molecule of sulfur dioxide when fully burned. This gives us a simple 1 to 1 mole ratio.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{S(s) + O}_2\text{(g) \rightarrow SO}_2\text{(g)}$$

**Find moles of sulfur present**

We are told the 100 dm3 of fuel contains 0.8346 g of sulfur in total. Convert this mass to moles.

Calculation rule:
$$\text{moles} = \frac{\text{mass}}{A_r}$$
$$\text{moles of S} = \frac{0.8346}{32.1} = 0.0260 \text{ mol}$$

**Link to moles of sulfur dioxide**

Because of the 1 to 1 ratio, maximum means all sulfur is converted, so moles of $\text{SO}_2$ formed equals moles of S burned.

$$\text{moles of SO}_2 = 0.0260 \text{ mol}$$

**Convert moles of gas to volume at room conditions**

At room conditions (room temperature and pressure), 1 mol of any gas occupies $24 \text{ dm}^3$, which is $24000 \text{ cm}^3$. Multiply to get the volume.

$$\text{volume} = \text{moles} \times 24000$$
$$\text{volume of SO}_2 = 0.0260 \times 24000 = 624 \text{ cm}^3$$

options.A: Incorrect. About 291 cm3 is roughly half the STP value. It comes from combining two errors, using $22.4 \text{ dm}^3$ for STP instead of $24 \text{ dm}^3$ for room conditions, and halving the moles.
options.B: Incorrect. 312 cm3 is exactly half the correct answer. This is the trap of dividing by 2, perhaps thinking two S atoms are needed for one $\text{SO}_2$, but the equation $\text{S + O}_2 \rightarrow \text{SO}_2$ is 1 to 1.
options.C: Incorrect. 582 cm3 is what you get if you use the old STP molar volume of $22400 \text{ cm}^3 \text{ mol}^{-1}$ ($0.0260 \times 22400$). The question specifically asks for room conditions, so you must use $24000 \text{ cm}^3 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.
options.D: Correct. Moles of S = 0.8346 / 32.1 = 0.0260 mol, so moles of $\text{SO}_2$ = 0.0260 mol. Volume at room conditions = 0.0260 x 24000 = 624 cm3.
